answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can bid, and gives each bonded identity the same bidding quota. A fake identity is no free island of capacity: a tide of 10,000 bots requires 10,000 bonds, tying up capital for a month. Splitting one bankroll across more names cannot raise its total quota without more collateral, so a plume of new accounts carries a measurable financing cost.
